text:
nik: Heads up - ap-south1 showing repeated tiny-fragment islands; scheduler is performing repeated eager-repacks and evicting small pods to defragment for large reserved gigs. Customers hitting queue jitter.
ravi: I saw that. The scheduler's eagerRepack flag is on for binpack policy; with mixed GPU shapes it ends up worse than leaving small islands.
sora: Can we flip to soft-preempt behavior? Instead of immediate eviction, prefer scheduling candidates that land in warm-pools or nodes with PreferNoSchedule soft taint.
kevin: operationally safest is a canary: 1) disable eagerRepack for one AZ, 2) increase warm-pool size by +25% for that AZ, 3) add a PreferNoSchedule taint on reserved nodes, and add tolerations to low-priority namespaces.
nik: propose timeline: apply canary now, watch 30m, roll forward if preempt_count drops >20% and pod_start_time improves.
ravi: sample commands: 
```bash
# canary scheduler patch
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap gpu-scheduler-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"eagerRepack":"false"}}'
# scale warm-pool
kubectl -n infra-scale scale deploy/warm-pool-apsouth --replicas=48 # +12 from 36
# soft taint reserved nodes
kubectl taint nodes -l reserved=large gpu_reserve=soft:PreferNoSchedule
```
sora: I'll add tolerations to the spot-batch namespace instead of touching customer deployments.
kevin: infra-bot, create runbook entry and start metrics collection for fit_failures, preempt_rate, pod_start_latency.
infra-bot: [runbook] id=r-45bb, owner=sora, cohort=ap-south1a, duration=30m. Metrics hooked.
nik: also keep an eye on cost delta from warm-pool extra nodes — should be minimal if warm-pool is used. Ravi, can you surface a quick estimate?
ravi: estimate: +12 warm-pool replicas in apsouth (~p4-like) ~ $1.6k/day if fully running. But if used for small pods it's offset by fewer preemptions and less reschedule overhead.
sora: warm-pool scaled to 48, tolerations applied to spot-batch. Canary config applied to 10% of schedulers.
infra-bot: [info] warm-pool scale complete. new size=48. canary apply id=c-311.
nik: early telemetry (10m): preempt_rate -15%, fit_failures -22%, pod_start_time median -90s -> -40s. promising.
kevin: good sign. Hold for 30m then decide. If improvement holds, plan: 1) flip eagerRepack off for the region during peak windows, 2) add warm-pool sizing recommendation to the autoscale controller, 3) RFC for a scheduler score that biases filling warm-pools before repacking.
ravi: agree. Also add a guard to limit eagerRepack to when fragmentation exceeds threshold. We should avoid binary on/off.
sora: noted. I'll collect traces and allocation logs and upload to shared folder.
nik: thanks team. If anyone sees negative side-effects (increased tail latency for big reserved jobs) we rollback immediately.
infra-bot: [alert] canary window complete: result=improved, next=scale-eval-and-rfc.
